evidence.quote: let allocation memberId (library: Library) : (Fine * FinePayment) list =
Settled = Accounts.settledBy payment.Member before library |> List.map (fun fine -> CopyId.value fine.Copy) }

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Tier 2 (Accounts.allocation, Accounts.settledBy) decides the new rules: payments go to fines oldest first, a fine is paid in full, in part or not at all, and a payment settles certain fines. The Tier 1 type FinePayment carries the result. Tier 3 Views only maps FinePayment to strings and calls settledBy. The CLI only formats the view, choosing between 'paid', 'paid X of Y' and 'unpaid' and adding the '(settled ...)' suffix when the list is non-empty. No Tier 3/4 site re-derives any of these rules.

evidence.quote: |> Result.map (fun (l, payment) -> l, Views.ofPayment library l payment)))

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effects. The settled-fines result is computed purely by comparing the before and after Library values inside the existing commit path. Tier 1/2 additions are pure functions over Library. Presentation only renders Tier 3 views.

evidence.quote: let paid = paymentsOf memberId library |> List.sumBy (fun payment -> payment.Amount)

ARC-REV-03.rationale: Allocation order and per-fine payment status are defined once, in Accounts.allocation. settledBy reuses it through paidInFull, and Views and the CLI reference those results. Both owed and allocation sum payments, but each uses the shared paymentsOf in the same Tier 2 module, so no rule or literal is copied into another tier.

evidence.quote: | Waived(approver, paid) -> WaivedBy(approver, (if paid > 0m then Some(money paid) else None)) })
let waive memberId copyId (approver: string) (library: Library) : Result<Library * Fine, LendingError> =
| Ok [ "borrow"; m; c ] -> UseCases.borrow ports m c |> render showBorrow

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The waiver rules all live in Tier 2: approver required, earliest fine for the copy with something unpaid, waived fines take no more payments and drop out of owed. The change also moves the borrowing block out of the CLI, which had its own 'fines - paid >= 5.00m' check, and into Loans.borrow through Accounts.isBlocked. That fixes an existing violation. However, Tier 3 Views re-derives part of the 'was anything paid on this fine' rule with its own 'paid > 0m' check, mirroring Tier 2's 'applied > 0m' test. This duplicates a predicate without contradicting it, so the score is 1.

evidence.quote: | Some waiver -> "waiver", record [ "approver", text waiver.Approver; "paidBefore", amount waiver.PaidBefore ]

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The new waive use case persists only through the existing commit/Store port, and Tier 2 Waivers.waive is pure. JSON encoding stays in the Tier 4 persistence adapter. The change also removes the CLI's direct ports.Store.Load() and its inline borrowing decision, so Tier 4 presentation no longer re-decides borrowing. No new effect appears below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: if paid > 0m then Some(money paid) else None

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The amount paid on a waived fine has two sources. It is saved as Waiver.PaidBefore when the fine is waived, and allocation recomputes it as 'applied' each time; account display uses the recomputed value. Because payments go oldest first and new fines come last, the two values agree, but the fact is still stated twice. The Tier 3 'paid > 0m' check also repeats Tier 2's paid/unpaid test. The copies agree, so the score is 1, not 0. The change improves AR-19 elsewhere by replacing the CLI's literal 5.00m with Policy.blockingBalance through Accounts.isBlocked.
